summary.intent: Drive Callisto (a Rust release manager for Cargo/npm/PyPI monorepos) toward v1 by working through the local NEXT-WORK plan (bug fixes, gaps, features) as signed, non-draft, stacked PRs the user merges.
summary.outcome: Opened and got merged dozens of PRs (SYS-RETRY, mixed-routing test, docs refresh, init/derive refactors, SYS-NAPI, E317-E320 changes, schemars 1.x, edition 2024, and more). Open at the end: #290 (A2 fix), #291 (E176 operation display), #292 (dependency update) and #248 (0.12.0 release PR). The last item, extracting the registry test tools into a composite action to fix the failing Release verify job, was committed and pushed but the PR was not yet confirmed open.

repo: Local tracking and handoff plans (.claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md) must never be committed or put in a PR; they are git-excluded via .git/info/exclude.
docs/errors.md carries an 'N numeric E#### codes total' count that conflicts across any PRs adding error rows, so they must be rebased in merge order.
The pre-commit hook runs fmt-check, so run cargo fmt --all before committing.
just lint runs clippy with -D clippy::unwrap_used on lib and bin targets only; use expect with an invariant message in non-test code.

The Release workflow's 'Verify release candidate' job lacked the verdaccio, pypiserver and cargo-http-registry install steps that the CI workflow has. The real-registry e2e tests fail rather than skip under CI, which broke every main push since #261 and blocked the 0.12.0 self-release.
Zizmor flags writes to GITHUB_PATH inside composite action files, so they need an ignore comment like the other suppressions in the repo.

schemars 1.x: wire types read via try_from need a JsonSchema derive, and output becomes draft 2020-12 ($defs, const). sha2 0.11 drops LowerHex on digests, comfy-table 8 renames load_preset to load_style, and toml 1.x str::parse::<Value> parses a single value rather than a document.
macOS bash lacks mapfile, so templates and tests run under it need a portable read loop.
AGENTS.md rules: no spec IDs in code, one changeset per user-visible topic, succinct docs, no emojis, never hard-wrap Markdown, no session links in commits or PRs.

code.finding: Inline Linux-only steps install verdaccio, pypiserver and cargo-http-registry for the real-registry e2e tests. They were extracted into a local composite action so the Release verify job can reuse them.

New module for A2: detects packages whose published version sits behind newer commits (E320) via commit_setting_version and version_at. Recovery is to detach to the version-setting sha and rerun release.
refuse_a_published_version_left_behind must skip in Preview when there is no origin, otherwise registry derive fails with E132.

workflow: The background-command notification 'exit code 0' only reflects the wrapper script; always read the log's own exit= line, which caught several real failures (fmt, clippy, test).
Prove with the real tool and reproduce the failure first; the real-binary reproduction plus mutation checks caught issues that fakes would have hidden.
Check pairwise merge conflicts (git merge-tree) before opening a batch of parallel PRs, and stack overlapping ones with gh stack link rather than leaving them to conflict.

The sandbox blocks heredocs, inline env, compound commands, GPG signing, cargo-registry writes and gh TLS; use script files written via Write and retry only the needed steps outside the sandbox, telling the user about /sandbox.
A plain git push can silently do nothing when the local branch name differs from the remote; push an explicit refspec.
When a rebase brings in tests from other PRs, re-scan for call patterns the PR's change invalidates, such as bare package specs after #281.

friction: Closed PR #201 mistakenly because the plan file was committed to a PR instead of staying local tracking.
Opened a batch of PRs off main without checking overlap, so seven pairs conflicted and the user had to point it out twice.
#281's hosted CI failed because tests merged from other PRs still used bare package specs.
Sandbox restrictions repeatedly forced workarounds: script files, running commands outside the sandbox, and failures with signed commits and gh TLS.
Misleading wrapper exit-code notifications hid real CI failures several times.
Dependabot #275 and #289 kept failing on cascading major bumps (schemars, then sha2, comfy-table, toml).
The Release workflow verify job has been broken on main since #261 without anyone noticing.
open_items: Confirm the PR for the composite-action fix is open and that the zizmor, workflow-contracts and action-pin checks pass; it unblocks release PR #248 (0.12.0).
A5: warn when the registry repository metadata does not match origin.
Floating v1 action tag with immutable versions; Intel mac and aarch64-linux binaries (policy-sensitive).
T12/T12-DX owner-run scratch-registry verification needs credentials; T08 is mostly shipped and the plan needs a note.
Post-1.0: OIDC trusted publishing and semver-checks on promised surfaces.
Owner acts: accept ADR 12 and cut 0.12.0.
The fuzz targets are only compile-checked and have not been run under libFuzzer; E176 was never reproduced against a real registry.
Stale branch deletion (docs/next-work-plan, docs/spec-rewrite, fix/native-resolution and about 35 local branches) awaits the user's per-branch decision.
W1 real-service credential check needs a decision on where it runs in CI; the W2 SYS-RETRY entries in the roadmap, plan JSON and guide still need follow-up edits.
